description: Retrieval-quality corpus for the memory recall pipeline (spec 08 §6) -- X-010, rebuilt by T21-18. Each entry carries an original-language variant (as a real user would write it) and a hand-translated English variant, so `cargo xtask memory-recall-bench` can seed and query either side and compare. Version 1.0.0 held 24 entries and 24 queries and could not discriminate: the dense leg ranked the expected entry first in 24/24 for every one of the five configurations, and both `store_en` and `both_en` sat at a perfect 1.000, so a ceiling was being asked to rank two things. It also gave only four queries per cross-language pair, which moved a per-pair hit@1 in steps of 0.25. This version is 200 entries -- 60 judged, one per query, at realistic length, and 140 thematically adjacent distractors that no query targets -- and 60 queries, 15 per language pair. `lang_pair` reads as (entry original language)-(query language). The relevance model is unchanged: single-relevant, one judgment per query.

entries.text_original: Для фьюжна поиска в Aurora остановились на RRF с k=45 вместо дефолтных 60. На прогоне бенчмарка из 49 запросов k=60 давал MRR на 0.03 хуже: лексическая нога слишком долго доминировала над плотной на коротких запросах в два-три слова, где точное совпадение термина почти всегда попадало в топ, а семантически близкий, но иначе сформулированный документ проваливался за пятую позицию. При k=45 вклад плотной ноги начинает сказываться раньше, и на длинных запросах разницы почти нет — проверяли отдельно на подвыборке из 14 запросов длиннее восьми слов, там MRR совпал с точностью до 0.005. Значение зафиксировано константой в конфиге фьюжна, менять его без нового прогона бенчмарка нельзя.
entries.text_english: For Aurora's search fusion we settled on RRF with k=45 instead of the default 60. Across the 49-query benchmark run k=60 scored 0.03 lower on MRR: the lexical leg kept dominating the dense leg for too long on short two- or three-word queries, where an exact term match almost always reached the top while a semantically close but differently worded document fell past position five. At k=45 the dense leg starts to tell earlier, and on long queries the difference all but vanishes — we checked that separately on a sub-sample of 14 queries longer than eight words, where MRR matched to within 0.005. The value is pinned as a constant in the fusion config and must not be changed without a fresh benchmark run.

entries.text_original: Флейковость в CI у Aurora объяснилась не гонкой в тестах, а тем, что Spotlight-индексатор macOS перехватывает exec каждого тестового бинарника на self-hosted раннере. В момент отказа замерено: XprotectService держал 37% CPU непрерывно почти пять часов, corespotlightd — 31%, syspolicyd — до 62%, при этом load average оставался около 2.75 и памяти хватало. То есть машина не была нагружена, но любой запуск бинарника вставал. Тестовый процесс залипал на _dyld_start с физическим следом в 96 КБ, не доходя даже до main; зависал и бинарник, успешно отработавший часом раньше, так что версия «свежий бинарь ещё не просканирован» не подтвердилась. Лечится исключением каталога сборки из индексации.
entries.text_english: Aurora's CI flakiness turned out not to be a test race at all: macOS's Spotlight indexer intercepts every test binary's exec on the self-hosted runner. Measured at the moment of failure, XprotectService held 37% CPU continuously for nearly five hours, corespotlightd 31%, syspolicyd up to 62%, while the load average stayed around 2.75 with memory to spare. The machine was not busy, yet every binary launch stalled. The test process hung at _dyld_start with a 96 KB physical footprint, never reaching main, and a binary that had run fine an hour earlier hung too, so "a fresh binary has not been scanned yet" did not hold up. The fix is excluding the build directory from indexing.

entries.text_original: В Aurora каждое сообщение коммита обязано ссылаться на тикет вида AURA-NNN в первой строке, иначе pre-commit хук его отклоняет. Правило появилось после того, как разбор инцидента с потерей платежей занял два дня только на то, чтобы связать изменения в трёх репозиториях с обсуждением, где решение принималось: половина коммитов не имела ни номера тикета, ни внятного текста. Хук проверяет только первую строку и только формат — содержательность остаётся на ревьюере. Исключение ровно одно: автоматические коммиты бота обновления зависимостей, они помечаются префиксом deps: и проходят мимо проверки, потому что тикета у них по построению нет.
entries.text_english: In Aurora, every commit message must reference a ticket in the AURA-NNN form on its first line, or the pre-commit hook rejects it. The rule appeared after an incident review into lost payments spent two full days just linking changes across three repositories back to the discussion where the decision had been made: half the commits carried neither a ticket number nor a meaningful description. The hook checks only the first line and only the format — substance stays with the reviewer. There is exactly one exception: the dependency-update bot's automatic commits, tagged with a deps: prefix, bypass the check because by construction they have no ticket.

entries.text_original: Кэш ответов в Aurora сделали на LRU с бюджетом 512 МБ, а не на LFU. LFU при пиковой нагрузке слишком долго держал горячие ключи прошлого инцидента и не отдавал место под новые: после февральского всплеска трафика ключи, набравшие счётчик за час аварии, вытеснялись почти сутки, и всё это время hit rate на актуальных запросах падал примерно вдвое. LRU в тех же условиях восстанавливался за десяток минут. Бюджет 512 МБ выбран не теоретически, а по замеру: на 256 МБ hit rate проседал до 61%, на 512 МБ — 84%, а дальнейшее удвоение давало прибавку меньше процента, что не оправдывает памяти на инстанс.
entries.text_english: Aurora's response cache uses LRU with a 512 MB budget instead of LFU. Under peak load LFU kept last incident's hot keys pinned far too long and never freed room for new ones: after February's traffic spike, keys that had built up a counter during the hour-long outage took nearly a full day to evict, and hit rate on current queries stayed roughly halved that whole time. LRU recovered in about ten minutes under the same conditions. The 512 MB budget was measured rather than theorised: at 256 MB hit rate sagged to 61%, at 512 MB it reached 84%, and doubling again added less than a percentage point, which does not justify the memory per instance.

entries.text_original: Сервис ingest-worker в Aurora падает с общей паникой без осмысленного кода ошибки, если на вход приходит пустой payload: обработчик разыменовывает Option без проверки, и стек в логе обрывается на unwrap внутри десериализатора. Внешне это выглядит как отказ всего пода, потому что supervisor перезапускает процесс, а очередь тут же отдаёт тот же пустой батч — получается цикл рестартов примерно раз в четыре секунды. Отличить от настоящей аварии по метрикам невозможно: и там и там растёт счётчик рестартов, а полезная нагрузка стоит. Пустые батчи приходят от старого клиента версии 1.4, который шлёт heartbeat тем же эндпоинтом.
entries.text_english: Aurora's ingest-worker service panics with no meaningful error code when it receives an empty payload: the handler dereferences an Option without checking it, and the logged stack trace stops at an unwrap inside the deserializer. From the outside it looks like the whole pod failed, because the supervisor restarts the process and the queue immediately hands back the same empty batch — a restart loop roughly every four seconds. Metrics cannot tell this apart from a real outage: both show a climbing restart counter and stalled throughput. The empty batches come from an old 1.4 client that sends its heartbeat through the same endpoint.

entries.text_original: Ротация учётных данных staging-базы в Aurora идёт строго в четыре шага. Сначала создать новый пароль в секрет-хранилище с суффиксом -next, не трогая текущий. Затем прогнать деплой, при котором сервис принимает оба пароля одновременно: приложение читает пару и пробует их по очереди, так что ни один активный пул соединений не рвётся. Третий шаг — дождаться, пока метрика подключений со старым паролем не упадёт до нуля и продержится там пятнадцать минут; это гарантирует, что переподключились и фоновые воркеры, которые держат соединение часами. Только после этого удалять старый пароль и снимать суффикс с нового. Пропуск третьего шага — самая частая причина ночных инцидентов на staging.
entries.text_english: Rotating Aurora's staging database credentials goes in exactly four steps. First create a new password in the secret store with a -next suffix, leaving the current one untouched. Then deploy a build where the service accepts both passwords at once: the application reads the pair and tries them in turn, so no live connection pool is torn down. Third, wait until the metric for connections using the old password drops to zero and stays there for fifteen minutes; that is what proves the background workers, which hold connections for hours, have reconnected too. Only then delete the old password and drop the suffix from the new one. Skipping the third step is the most common cause of overnight staging incidents.

entries.text_original: До конца третьего квартала нужно перевести legacy-сервис report-gen в Aurora с Python 2 на Python 3, иначе он останется без патчей безопасности после того, как базовый образ уйдёт из поддержки. Основная работа не в синтаксисе, а в двух местах: самописный сериализатор отчётов полагается на порядок ключей в словаре, который в Python 2 был другим, и библиотека выгрузки в SFTP не имеет версии под Python 3 вовсе, её придётся заменить. Оценка — три недели, из них неделя на сверку отчётов байт в байт со старой версией: бухгалтерия принимает только полное совпадение, потому что итоговые суммы уходят во внешнюю систему.
entries.text_english: By the end of Q3, Aurora's legacy report-gen service must move off Python 2 onto Python 3, or it will stop receiving security patches once the base image leaves support. The bulk of the work is not syntax but two specific places: the home-grown report serializer relies on dictionary key ordering, which differed under Python 2, and the SFTP upload library has no Python 3 release at all and must be replaced outright. The estimate is three weeks, one of which goes to comparing reports byte for byte against the old version: finance accepts nothing short of an exact match, because the totals feed an external system.

entries.text_original: Подозреваем, что утечка памяти в session-cache Aurora вызвана незакрытыми WebSocket-хендлами: количество открытых файловых дескрипторов растёт линейно с числом подключившихся за сутки клиентов и не падает после их отключения. Косвенно это подтверждает форма графика — ступеньки ровно в моменты пиков подключений, без спада ночью, тогда как при утечке в кэше значений рост шёл бы вместе с объёмом данных, а не с числом сессий. Проверить можно дёшево: снять lsof на поде, прожившем больше двенадцати часов, и посмотреть, сколько сокетов в состоянии CLOSE_WAIT. Пока это гипотеза, приоритет расследования — средний, потому что под перезапускается по памяти раз в двое суток и пользователи этого не замечают.
entries.text_english: We suspect the memory leak in Aurora's session-cache comes from unclosed WebSocket handles: the open file descriptor count grows linearly with the number of clients that connected during the day and never falls after they disconnect. The shape of the graph is indirect support — steps exactly at connection peaks, with no overnight decline, whereas a leak in the value cache would track data volume rather than session count. Checking it is cheap: take lsof on a pod that has been up more than twelve hours and count sockets sitting in CLOSE_WAIT. This is still a hypothesis and the investigation is medium priority, because the pod restarts on memory roughly every two days and users do not notice.

entries.text_original: Команда договорилась не хранить refresh_token в LocalStorage фронтенда Aurora, только в httpOnly cookie. После аудита выяснилось, что любой подключённый скрипт сторонней аналитики читает LocalStorage целиком, и на странице оформления заказа таких скриптов оказалось три, включая один, подключаемый через тег-менеджер без ревью. Access-token живёт в памяти вкладки и не переживает перезагрузку — это осознанная плата за то, что его нельзя вытащить скриптом. Cookie выставляется с SameSite=Lax и Secure, домен ограничен поддоменом api, чтобы её не видели статические хосты. Запрет действует и на мобильный веб-вью, там роль LocalStorage играет общий с приложением контейнер.
entries.text_english: The team agreed not to store refresh_token in Aurora's frontend LocalStorage, only in an httpOnly cookie. An audit found that any installed third-party analytics script reads LocalStorage wholesale, and the checkout page carried three such scripts, including one injected through the tag manager without review. The access token lives in tab memory and does not survive a reload — a deliberate price for making it unreachable from script. The cookie is set with SameSite=Lax and Secure, scoped to the api subdomain so static hosts never see it. The ban covers the mobile web view too, where the container shared with the app plays LocalStorage's role.

entries.text_original: Очередь уведомлений в Aurora решили перевести с RabbitMQ на NATS JetStream. Повторные доставки из dead-letter очереди RabbitMQ дублировали пользовательские уведомления: сообщение уходило в DLQ по таймауту получателя, автоматический возврат клал его обратно в основную очередь, а исходный получатель к тому моменту успевал обработать его успешно. За квартал набралось около четырёхсот жалоб на повторные письма, и все они пришлись на два всплеска нагрузки. JetStream выбран за явное подтверждение с дедупликацией по идентификатору сообщения в окне, а не за пропускную способность — по ней RabbitMQ хватало с запасом. Миграция поэтапная: сначала уведомления о доставке, потом платежи.
entries.text_english: Aurora's notification queue is moving from RabbitMQ to NATS JetStream. Redeliveries out of RabbitMQ's dead-letter queue were duplicating user-facing notifications: a message went to the DLQ on consumer timeout, the automatic return put it back on the main queue, and by then the original consumer had finished processing it successfully. Roughly four hundred complaints about duplicate emails accumulated over a quarter, all of them during two load spikes. JetStream was chosen for explicit acknowledgement with message-id deduplication inside a window, not for throughput — RabbitMQ had throughput to spare. The migration is staged: delivery notifications first, payments second.

entries.text_original: В сервисе pdf-render Aurora нашли баг: кириллические имена файлов ломают вложения в письмах, потому что заголовок Content-Disposition кодируется без RFC 5987, и почтовый клиент получает байты в неопределённой кодировке. У получателя вложение приходит с именем вида ______.pdf либо, у части клиентов, вовсе теряет расширение и не открывается по двойному клику. Латинские имена проходят нормально, поэтому баг не видели полгода — он всплыл только когда отчёты стали именовать по названию контрагента. Обходной путь до исправления: транслитерировать имя на стороне вызывающего сервиса, но это теряет информацию и годится только как временная мера.
entries.text_english: A bug was found in Aurora's pdf-render service: Cyrillic file names break email attachments because the Content-Disposition header is encoded without RFC 5987, so the mail client receives bytes in an undefined encoding. Recipients see an attachment named something like ______.pdf or, in some clients, one that loses its extension entirely and will not open on a double click. Latin names pass through fine, which is why the bug went unseen for six months — it surfaced only once reports began to be named after the counterparty. The workaround until it is fixed is to transliterate the name in the calling service, but that loses information and is strictly temporary.

entries.text_original: Все миграции схемы в Aurora обязаны быть обратимыми: down-миграция это не опциональная часть PR, ревьюер отклоняет любую миграцию без неё, даже если автор уверен, что откатывать не придётся. Правило пережило два обсуждения и осталось, потому что оба раза, когда откат реально понадобился, его писали в спешке под нагрузкой инцидента. Для необратимых по сути операций — например, удаления колонки с данными — down-миграция обязана восстанавливать структуру и явно документировать, что содержимое не восстанавливается; пустая заглушка с комментарием не принимается. Проверка частично автоматизирована: CI прогоняет up, down и снова up на копии схемы.
entries.text_english: Every schema migration in Aurora must be reversible: a down-migration is not an optional part of the PR, and a reviewer rejects any migration that lacks one, even when the author is certain no rollback will ever be needed. The rule survived two rounds of debate because on both occasions a rollback was actually required, it had to be written in a hurry under incident pressure. For operations that are inherently irreversible — dropping a column with data, say — the down-migration must restore the structure and document explicitly that the contents are not restored; an empty stub with a comment is not accepted. The check is partly automated: CI runs up, down and up again against a copy of the schema.

entries.text_original: Идемпотентность платежей в Aurora решили держать на ключе, который присылает клиент, а не на хеше тела запроса. Хеш казался удобнее — не нужно менять контракт, — но он ломается на ретраях, где клиент добавляет поле с меткой времени попытки: тело меняется, хеш другой, платёж проходит дважды. Ключ хранится в отдельной таблице с TTL в сутки и уникальным индексом, повторный запрос с тем же ключом возвращает сохранённый ответ, не трогая баланс. Плата за это — обязательное поле в API и явная ошибка, если клиент его не прислал; на переходный период три месяца сервис принимал запросы без ключа, логируя предупреждение.
entries.text_english: Aurora's payment idempotency is keyed on a client-supplied key rather than on a hash of the request body. The hash looked more convenient — no contract change — but it breaks on retries where the client appends a field with the attempt's timestamp: the body differs, the hash differs, and the payment goes through twice. The key is stored in its own table with a one-day TTL and a unique index; a repeat request with the same key returns the stored response without touching any balance. The price is a mandatory API field and an explicit error when a client omits it; for a three-month transition the service accepted keyless requests while logging a warning.

entries.text_original: Поиск по клиентам в Aurora перестаёт находить компании, в названии которых есть кавычки-ёлочки, потому что нормализатор запроса вырезает их как пунктуацию, а индексатор при записи сохранял как есть. Расхождение появилось при обновлении токенизатора: раньше обе стороны использовали одну функцию, потом индексатор переехал на новую версию, а запросный путь остался на старой. Практически это значит, что «Ромашка» находится по слову ромашка, но не находится по полному названию с кавычками, скопированному из договора — а именно так его чаще всего и вставляют. Затронуто около 4% карточек клиентов, все с юридическими названиями.
entries.text_english: Aurora's customer search stops finding companies whose names contain guillemet quotes, because the query normalizer strips them as punctuation while the indexer stored them verbatim. The mismatch appeared during a tokenizer upgrade: both sides used to share one function, then the indexer moved to a new version and the query path stayed on the old one. In practice this means a company written with guillemets is found by the bare word but not by the full name copied out of a contract — which is exactly how people paste it. Roughly 4% of customer records are affected, all of them with legal-form names.

entries.text_original: Публичные API Aurora версионируются только через путь (/v1, /v2), заголовок Accept для версионирования не используется. Причина практическая: заголовок теряется на трёх прокси из четырёх в инфраструктуре партнёров, и мы дважды получали инциденты, где запрос молча уходил в версию по умолчанию и возвращал другую форму ответа. Версия в пути видна в логах, в трассировке и в кэш-ключе без дополнительной настройки. Внутри одной версии допускаются только совместимые изменения: добавление необязательного поля можно, изменение типа или смысла существующего — нет, для этого поднимается новая версия целиком.
entries.text_english: Aurora's public APIs are versioned through the path (/v1, /v2) only; the Accept header is not used for versioning. The reason is practical: the header is dropped by three proxies out of four in partner infrastructure, and we twice had incidents where a request silently fell through to the default version and returned a different response shape. A version in the path is visible in logs, in traces and in the cache key with no extra configuration. Within one version only compatible changes are allowed: adding an optional field is fine, changing the type or meaning of an existing one is not, and calls for a whole new version.

entries.text_original: Разбор жалобы на неверный расчёт скидки в Aurora начинается не с кода, а с восстановления входных данных. Порядок такой: взять номер заказа, найти в архиве событий снимок корзины на момент расчёта, поднять версию правил скидок, действовавшую в ту минуту, и прогнать калькулятор в песочнице на этих трёх вещах. Только если результат песочницы совпал с тем, что увидел клиент, имеет смысл смотреть в правила; если не совпал — расхождение в данных, а не в логике, и дальше идти надо в сторону кэша цен. Шаг с версией правил пропускают чаще всего, а он и объясняет большинство жалоб: правила меняются несколько раз в неделю.
entries.text_english: Investigating a complaint about a wrong discount in Aurora starts with reconstructing the inputs, not with the code. The order is: take the order number, find the cart snapshot at calculation time in the event archive, pull the discount-rule version that was in force that minute, and run the calculator in a sandbox against those three things. Only if the sandbox result matches what the customer saw is there any point looking at the rules; if it does not, the discrepancy is in the data rather than the logic, and the next place to look is the price cache. The rule-version step is the one most often skipped, and it explains most complaints: the rules change several times a week.

entries.text_original: Есть подозрение, что рост числа отменённых заказов в Aurora связан не с ценами, а с тем, что таймер удержания товара на складе идёт от момента создания заказа, а не от момента успешной оплаты. При медленной оплате картой удержание истекает раньше, чем приходит подтверждение, товар уходит другому покупателю, и заказ отменяется автоматически с формулировкой про отсутствие на складе. Косвенное подтверждение: доля отмен вдвое выше у способов оплаты с редиректом на страницу банка, где типичное время до подтверждения около двух минут против пятнадцати секунд у сохранённой карты. Проверяется сравнением распределения времени оплаты у отменённых и успешных заказов.
entries.text_english: There is a suspicion that Aurora's rising order-cancellation count has nothing to do with pricing and everything to do with the warehouse hold timer running from order creation rather than from successful payment. With a slow card payment the hold expires before confirmation arrives, the item goes to another buyer, and the order is cancelled automatically with an out-of-stock message. Indirect support: the cancellation share is twice as high for payment methods that redirect to a bank page, where time to confirmation is typically about two minutes against fifteen seconds for a stored card. It can be checked by comparing payment-time distributions for cancelled and successful orders.

entries.text_original: Нужно вынести генерацию превью изображений из монолита Aurora в отдельный сервис до начала сезонной нагрузки. Сейчас превью считаются синхронно в том же процессе, что обслуживает карточку товара, и на загрузке каталога поставщиком это съедает до 70% CPU пода, из-за чего страдают обычные запросы. Отдельный сервис позволит масштабировать превью независимо и ограничить их долю ресурсов. Работа оценена в две недели и включает миграцию уже сгенерированных превью: их около одиннадцати миллионов, переносить придётся фоново, с двойной записью на время перехода, иначе первый же промах кэша даст всплеск на холодном сервисе.
entries.text_english: Image preview generation must be moved out of Aurora's monolith into its own service before the seasonal load starts. Previews are currently computed synchronously in the same process that serves the product page, and during a supplier catalogue upload that eats up to 70% of the pod's CPU, degrading ordinary requests. A separate service allows previews to scale independently and caps their share of resources. The work is estimated at two weeks and includes migrating the previews already generated: there are about eleven million of them, they have to move in the background with dual writes during the transition, or the first cache miss will spike a cold service.

entries.text_original: Экспорт аналитики в Aurora считает выручку по дате создания заказа, а бухгалтерия — по дате отгрузки, поэтому месячные итоги двух отчётов никогда не сходятся и не должны. Расхождение стабильно держится в пределах трёх-четырёх процентов и целиком объясняется заказами, созданными в последние дни месяца и отгруженными в начале следующего. Это не баг: обе даты нужны, у них разные потребители, и попытка свести их в один отчёт уже предпринималась — она провалилась, потому что бухгалтерии нужен момент перехода права собственности, а маркетингу момент решения о покупке. В отчётах обе даты подписаны явно, чтобы никто не сравнивал их напрямую.
entries.text_english: Aurora's analytics export counts revenue by order creation date while finance counts it by shipment date, so the monthly totals of the two reports never agree and are not meant to. The gap stays steadily within three to four percent and is entirely explained by orders created in the last days of a month and shipped early in the next. This is not a bug: both dates are needed, they have different consumers, and an attempt to merge them into one report has already been made and failed, because finance needs the moment ownership transfers and marketing needs the moment the purchase decision was made. Both dates are labelled explicitly in the reports so nobody compares them directly.

entries.text_original: Хранение файлов пользователей в Aurora перевели на S3-совместимое объектное хранилище с шифрованием на стороне сервера, отказавшись от шифрования на стороне приложения. Приложенческое шифрование выглядело безопаснее, но требовало держать ключи в процессе, который и так обрабатывает недоверенный ввод, и полностью ломало возможность отдавать файлы по подписанной ссылке — каждый байт пришлось бы проксировать через сервис. Замер показал, что проксирование добавляло около 40 мс к медиане и делало исходящий трафик сервиса в шесть раз больше. Ключи теперь в KMS, ротация раз в квартал, доступ к расшифровке ограничен ролью, которую сервис получает по короткоживущему токену.
entries.text_english: Aurora's user file storage moved to S3-compatible object storage with server-side encryption, dropping application-side encryption. Encrypting in the application looked safer but required keeping keys inside a process that already handles untrusted input, and it broke signed-URL delivery entirely — every byte would have had to be proxied through the service. Measurement showed proxying added about 40 ms to the median and multiplied the service's outbound traffic sixfold. Keys now live in KMS, rotate quarterly, and decryption access is limited to a role the service assumes through a short-lived token.

entries.text_original: Мобильное приложение Aurora показывает пустой экран истории заказов, если у пользователя больше пятисот заказов: пагинация на клиенте запрашивает все страницы разом и упирается в таймаут шлюза в тридцать секунд, а обработчик ошибки трактует таймаут как пустой ответ. На вебе того же не происходит, потому что там пагинация серверная. Затронуто меньше процента аккаунтов, но это ровно те аккаунты, которые чаще всего пишут в поддержку — оптовые покупатели. Временное решение на стороне сервера: жёсткий лимит в двести заказов на ответ с явным признаком, что данные обрезаны, чтобы клиент показал хотя бы часть.
entries.text_english: Aurora's mobile app shows an empty order-history screen for users with more than five hundred orders: client-side pagination requests every page at once, hits the gateway's thirty-second timeout, and the error handler treats the timeout as an empty response. The web app is unaffected because its pagination is server-side. Fewer than one percent of accounts are affected, but they are precisely the accounts that contact support most — wholesale buyers. The temporary server-side fix is a hard limit of two hundred orders per response with an explicit truncation flag, so the client at least shows part of the list.

entries.text_original: Логи в Aurora пишутся только структурно, в JSON, и любое поле, способное содержать пользовательский ввод, обязано проходить через редактор персональных данных перед записью. Свободный текст в логе запрещён не из вкуса, а потому что дважды в него попадали номера телефонов из формы обратной связи, и оба раза это выяснялось при выгрузке логов подрядчику. Список полей, считающихся чувствительными, лежит рядом с кодом редактора и обязателен к обновлению в том же PR, что добавляет новое поле в API. Ревьюер имеет право отклонить PR, где новое поле логируется без явного решения — редактировать его или нет.
entries.text_english: Aurora's logs are written structurally, as JSON, and any field capable of holding user input must pass through the personal-data redactor before it is written. Free text in a log line is banned not as a matter of taste but because phone numbers from the feedback form landed in one twice, and both times it came to light while exporting logs to a contractor. The list of fields considered sensitive lives next to the redactor's code and must be updated in the same PR that adds a new API field. A reviewer may reject a PR where a new field is logged without an explicit decision about whether to redact it.

entries.text_original: Ввод нового поставщика в каталог Aurora проходит через карантинную витрину. Сначала его товары загружаются в отдельное пространство имён, невидимое покупателям, и там прогоняется автоматическая проверка: обязательные атрибуты, дубли по штрихкоду с уже существующими товарами, диапазон цен относительно медианы категории. Затем товарный менеджер вручную смотрит выборку в пятьдесят позиций, отобранную не случайно, а по краям распределения цены. Публикация возможна только после обеих проверок, и она пакетная — отдельные товары из карантина не выпускаются, чтобы в выдаче не оказалось половины каталога поставщика без второй половины.
entries.text_english: Onboarding a new supplier into Aurora's catalogue goes through a quarantine storefront. Their goods are first loaded into a separate namespace invisible to buyers, where an automatic check runs: mandatory attributes, barcode duplicates against existing products, and price range relative to the category median. A category manager then reviews a sample of fifty items by hand, chosen not at random but from the tails of the price distribution. Publication is possible only after both checks and happens in one batch — individual items are never released from quarantine, so search never ends up with half a supplier's catalogue and not the other half.

entries.text_original: Предполагаем, что всплески задержки в сервисе рекомендаций Aurora вызваны не самой моделью, а перезагрузкой словаря признаков: он читается с диска целиком под глобальной блокировкой, и на время чтения все запросы выстраиваются в очередь. Совпадение по времени точное — пики приходятся на минуты, кратные пятнадцати, а именно так настроен интервал обновления словаря. Размер словаря вырос за полгода втрое, и чтение теперь занимает около 800 мс против 250 мс весной, что как раз объясняет, почему проблема стала заметна недавно. Проверяется просто: временно увеличить интервал до часа и посмотреть, станут ли пики реже ровно вчетверо.
entries.text_english: We suspect the latency spikes in Aurora's recommendation service come not from the model itself but from reloading the feature dictionary: it is read from disk in full under a global lock, and every request queues up for the duration. The timing lines up exactly — the spikes fall on minutes divisible by fifteen, which is precisely the dictionary's refresh interval. The dictionary has tripled in size over six months and the read now takes about 800 ms against 250 ms in the spring, which explains why the problem only became noticeable recently. It is easy to test: raise the interval to an hour temporarily and see whether the spikes become exactly four times rarer.

entries.text_original: Для внутренней аутентификации между сервисами Aurora выбрали mTLS вместо подписанных JWT. Решающим оказался не уровень защиты, а операционная сторона: отзыв скомпрометированного JWT требовал бы списка отзыва и его распространения по всем сервисам, тогда как сертификат отзывается в одном месте и перестаёт работать в течение времени жизни сессии. Дополнительно mTLS снимает вопрос о том, где хранить секрет подписи и как его ротировать без окна, в котором валидны два ключа. Плата — усложнение локальной разработки: разработчику нужен свой сертификат, и для этого сделан отдельный CLI, выдающий сертификат на восемь часов.
entries.text_english: Aurora chose mTLS over signed JWTs for service-to-service authentication. The decisive factor was operational rather than cryptographic: revoking a compromised JWT would require a revocation list and its distribution to every service, whereas a certificate is revoked in one place and stops working within the session lifetime. mTLS also removes the question of where to keep the signing secret and how to rotate it without a window in which two keys are valid. The price is more awkward local development: a developer needs their own certificate, and a dedicated CLI was written to issue one valid for eight hours.

entries.text_original: Импорт прайс-листов в Aurora молча теряет строки, где цена записана с пробелом как разделителем тысяч: парсер приводит такую строку к нулю, а валидатор пропускает нули, считая их допустимой ценой для акционных позиций. Внешне импорт завершается успехом, в отчёте загрузки стоит полное число строк, и расхождение всплывает только когда товар появляется в выдаче с ценой ноль. Формат с пробелом присылают два поставщика из сорока, оба выгружают из одной бухгалтерской системы. Правильное поведение — отклонять строку с явной ошибкой, а не молча подставлять ноль; нулевая цена должна выражаться отдельным признаком, а не значением.
entries.text_english: Aurora's price-list import silently loses rows where the price uses a space as a thousands separator: the parser coerces such a string to zero, and the validator lets zeros through, treating them as a legitimate price for promotional items. From the outside the import succeeds, the upload report shows the full row count, and the discrepancy surfaces only when a product appears in search priced at zero. Two suppliers out of forty send that format, both exporting from the same accounting system. The correct behaviour is to reject the row with an explicit error rather than quietly substituting zero; a zero price should be expressed by a separate flag, not by the value.

entries.text_original: Фича-флаги в Aurora обязаны иметь дату истечения в момент создания, и она не может быть дальше трёх месяцев. Флаг без даты не проходит проверку при деплое. Правило появилось после ревизии, которая нашла в коде сорок семь флагов, из них тридцать один включён на сто процентов больше года и по сути является мёртвым ветвлением, а два — выключены и защищают код, который больше не компилируется, если ветку включить. Продление возможно, но требует явного PR с обоснованием, и это сознательно сделано неудобным: продлить проще всего тогда, когда флаг действительно нужен, а в остальных случаях дешевле удалить ветку.
entries.text_english: Feature flags in Aurora must carry an expiry date at creation, and it cannot be more than three months out. A flag without a date fails the deploy check. The rule came out of an audit that found forty-seven flags in the codebase: thirty-one had been at one hundred percent for over a year and were effectively dead branches, and two were off and guarding code that no longer compiles if the branch is enabled. Extension is possible but requires an explicit PR with a justification, and that friction is deliberate: extending is easiest when the flag is genuinely needed, and otherwise deleting the branch is cheaper.

entries.text_original: Перевод трафика Aurora между регионами делается только через изменение веса в DNS с шагом не больше двадцати процентов и паузой в десять минут между шагами. Резкое переключение пробовали дважды, и оба раза холодный кэш в целевом регионе давал всплеск задержки на порядок: база принимала лавину запросов, которые в норме гасятся кэшем, и уходила в очередь. Пауза нужна именно на прогрев, а не на наблюдение — десять минут выбраны по времени, за которое hit rate в целевом регионе выходит на плато. Откат делается тем же шагом в обратную сторону; резкий откат так же вреден, как резкое переключение, и это менее очевидно.
entries.text_english: Shifting Aurora's traffic between regions is done only by changing DNS weights, in steps of no more than twenty percent with a ten-minute pause between them. A hard cutover was tried twice, and both times the cold cache in the target region produced an order-of-magnitude latency spike: the database took an avalanche of requests that the cache normally absorbs and fell behind. The pause is for warming, not for observation — ten minutes is the time it takes hit rate in the target region to plateau. Rollback uses the same step size in reverse; an abrupt rollback is just as harmful as an abrupt cutover, and that is the less obvious half.

entries.text_original: Нужно заменить самописный планировщик отложенных задач в Aurora на очередь с отложенной доставкой до конца года. Текущий планировщик хранит задачи в таблице и опрашивает её раз в секунду, из-за чего при десяти тысячах отложенных задач опрос сам по себе занимает половину секунды и создаёт постоянную нагрузку на реплику. Дополнительная проблема — отсутствие гарантии однократного выполнения при развёртывании двух инстансов: блокировка берётся оптимистично, и в редких случаях задача выполняется дважды. Оценка — три недели, включая перенос примерно шестидесяти тысяч уже запланированных задач без изменения времени их срабатывания.
entries.text_english: Aurora's home-grown deferred-task scheduler must be replaced with a queue offering delayed delivery before the end of the year. The current scheduler keeps tasks in a table and polls it once a second, so with ten thousand deferred tasks the poll alone takes half a second and puts constant load on the replica. A second problem is the lack of an exactly-once guarantee when two instances are deployed: the lock is taken optimistically, and in rare cases a task runs twice. The estimate is three weeks, including migrating roughly sixty thousand already-scheduled tasks without changing when they fire.

entries.text_original: Есть версия, что рост числа ошибок 409 в API заказов Aurora вызван не конкуренцией пользователей, а повторами самого мобильного клиента: он ретраит запрос по таймауту в пять секунд, а сервер в это время всё ещё держит транзакцию, и второй запрос натыкается на оптимистическую блокировку первого. Подтверждение косвенное, но сильное: доля 409 растёт ровно в те часы, когда медиана времени ответа переваливает за четыре секунды, то есть подходит к клиентскому таймауту. Настоящая конкуренция дала бы равномерное распределение по времени суток. Проверяется сопоставлением идентификатора запроса у пар 409 — если у них общий идентификатор попытки, версия верна.
entries.text_english: One theory is that the rise in 409 errors on Aurora's order API comes not from users competing but from the mobile client retrying itself: it retries on a five-second timeout while the server still holds the transaction, and the second request runs into the first one's optimistic lock. The support is indirect but strong: the 409 share climbs in exactly the hours when median response time passes four seconds, that is, approaches the client timeout. Genuine contention would be spread evenly across the day. It can be checked by matching request identifiers across 409 pairs — if they share an attempt id, the theory holds.

entries.text_original: Aurora's API gateway rate-limits with a token bucket, 100 requests per second per client, chosen over a sliding window because it tolerates short legitimate bursts without rejecting them. Partner integrations routinely open a batch of twenty parallel calls at the top of the minute; under a sliding window those pushed the counter past the limit and produced 429s for traffic that was well inside the hourly budget. The bucket refills continuously, so a burst borrows against the next second rather than being denied. The limit is per client identifier rather than per IP: several of the largest partners share an egress address, and per-IP limiting punished them collectively for one integration's mistake.

entries.text_original: The billing-exporter job in Aurora silently drops rows once the generated CSV exceeds 2 GB: the writer hits a platform file-size limit and swallows the resulting error, so the job reports success with a truncated file. Nothing in the metrics distinguishes a complete export from a cut one, because the row counter is incremented before the write rather than after it. The threshold is reached only in months with a full billing cycle for the largest tenant, which is why it went unnoticed for three quarters. Downstream reconciliation caught it, not the pipeline: the finance system's total came out short by exactly the tail of the alphabet, since rows are ordered by customer name.

entries.text_original: Every Terraform module in Aurora must pin its provider version exactly, with no ~> ranges. An unpinned provider once auto-upgraded mid-apply and silently changed a default: a security group that had allowed a specific CIDR was recreated with the provider's new default of none, and an internal service lost connectivity for forty minutes during what was supposed to be a no-op plan. Pinning is enforced by a policy check in CI rather than by review, because the failure mode is invisible in a diff — the module source does not change, only what the provider does with it. Upgrades are deliberate PRs that bump one provider at a time and re-run plan against every environment.

entries.text_original: For the CDC pipeline, Aurora picked PostgreSQL logical replication over Debezium. Debezium's Kafka Connect dependency would have added a whole cluster to operate for a single consumer, and the team that would have owned it is the same one already carrying the search indexer. Logical replication needs no extra moving parts: the downstream service subscribes directly and keeps its own replication slot. The known cost is accepted deliberately — an abandoned slot pins WAL on the primary, so a monitoring rule alerts when slot lag passes 5 GB, and a runbook covers dropping a slot whose consumer is gone for good. Debezium remains the fallback if a second, differently shaped consumer ever appears.

entries.text_original: Aurora's auth-service returns HTTP 500 instead of 401 when a JWT is well-formed but expired: the expiry check throws before the handler's own error mapping runs, so the framework's default handler answers instead. Clients treat 500 as retryable, so an expired session turns into a retry storm rather than a redirect to login — one mobile release amplified a single user's expired token into roughly two hundred requests per minute. A malformed token is handled correctly and returns 401, which is why the bug survived review: the obvious test case passes. The fix is to move the expiry check inside the mapped region, not to special-case the exception type.

entries.text_original: To roll back a failed canary deploy of Aurora's checkout-api: freeze the canary's traffic weight at 0 first, wait for in-flight requests to drain, then revert the deployment object, and only then delete the canary pods. Deleting the pods first is the mistake people make under pressure — it returns in-flight checkout requests as connection resets, and a reset during payment capture leaves the order in a state the reconciliation job has to clean up by hand. Draining is not instantaneous because the longest checkout call waits on an external payment provider, so the runbook says to wait for the in-flight gauge to read zero rather than to wait a fixed number of seconds.

entries.text_original: Add OpenTelemetry tracing to Aurora's notification-dispatcher service. Right now an incident review has no way to tell which upstream event triggered a given outgoing notification: the dispatcher logs the notification it sent and the queue logs the message it delivered, but nothing carries an identifier across the boundary. During the duplicate-email incident that cost two days of investigation, correlating the two sides had to be done by timestamp and recipient, which is ambiguous precisely when volume is high. The work is small — propagate the trace context through the queue message headers and start a span per dispatch — but it needs the queue migration to land first.

entries.text_original: The Friday p99 latency spike on Aurora's API gateway is suspected to correlate with the weekly analytics batch job, which reads from the same read replica the gateway uses for its permission lookups. The spike lands within a few minutes of the job's start every week and lasts roughly as long as the job's heaviest query, which scans a year of order history without a covering index. The gateway's own throughput is flat across the spike, which argues against a traffic cause. Confirming it is a matter of moving the batch job to its own replica for one week and comparing; the replica exists already and is currently used only for ad-hoc queries.

entries.text_original: The team picked feature flags via LaunchDarkly for Aurora instead of a home-grown config service. The home-grown option would have needed its own audit trail, targeting rules and a UI that non-engineers could use without a deploy, and the estimate for that came to about six engineer-weeks before any flag existed. The decision is explicitly revisitable: the contract is one year, and the code touches the vendor only through a thin internal interface with a file-backed implementation used in tests, so a move back is bounded work rather than a rewrite. What tipped it was targeting by customer segment, which the home-grown version had not even been designed for.

entries.text_original: Aurora's search-indexer re-embeds every document on a config reload, even documents whose content did not change at all: the reload path never checks the stored content hash and rebuilds the index from scratch. A reload is triggered by any change to the indexing configuration, including changes that cannot affect embeddings, such as the log level or the batch size. A full rebuild costs about forty minutes of GPU time and, more importantly, holds the write lock long enough that incremental updates queue behind it. Nobody noticed for months because reloads were rare; they became frequent when the batch size was made tunable at runtime.

entries.text_original: To request a temporary elevated role in Aurora's admin panel: open a request against the on-call approver, state the exact action and a time-box, and let the grant expire on its own rather than revoking it by hand. The time-box is mandatory and capped at four hours; anything longer is a sign the action belongs in a script that runs with its own service identity. Approvals are logged with the stated reason, and the weekly access review reads those reasons rather than the grants themselves, because a grant without a reason tells the reviewer nothing. Self-approval is blocked technically, not by policy, so it cannot be skipped during an incident.

entries.text_original: Onboarding drop-off in Aurora is suspected to come from the mandatory SSO step timing out over VPN: the timeout is fixed at 8 seconds, and VPN-routed logins from the two largest corporate customers measure between 6 and 11 seconds at the median. The drop-off is concentrated in accounts whose email domain matches those customers, which is what makes network conditions a better explanation than form design. A user who times out sees a generic error with no retry affordance, so the funnel records an abandonment rather than a failure. The cheap test is raising the timeout to 20 seconds for one domain and comparing completion rates over a week.

entries.text_original: Aurora stores monetary amounts as integer minor units rather than as decimals. The decision followed a rounding incident where a discount applied to a decimal price produced a half-cent that different services rounded in different directions, so the order total and the invoice total disagreed by one cent on about one order in four thousand. Integers make the rounding point explicit: it happens once, in the pricing service, and every consumer downstream receives an exact value. The cost is that every boundary must carry the currency alongside the number, since minor units are meaningless without it, and that is enforced by the shared money type rather than by convention.

entries.text_original: Aurora's warehouse sync marks an item as available the moment the supplier's feed lists it, without waiting for physical receipt, and that is the source of most oversell incidents. The feed reports what the supplier has committed to ship, not what is on the shelf, and for two suppliers the gap between those runs three to five days. When a customer orders inside that window the order is accepted and then cancelled at picking, which reads to the customer as a bait-and-switch. The field the sync should use exists in the feed but is optional, and those two suppliers do not populate it, which is why the naive mapping was written in the first place.

entries.text_original: Database access in Aurora goes through repository types only; no service constructs SQL inline. The rule is about auditability rather than style: when a personal-data request arrives, answering which code paths can read a given column has to be a search over a bounded set of files, not over the whole codebase. Repositories are also the single place where row-level scoping by tenant is applied, and a query written inline has historically forgotten it — the one production data leak in this system's history came from exactly that. Raw SQL is permitted inside a repository, and encouraged where an ORM would obscure the query plan.

entries.text_original: Restoring a single tenant's data in Aurora never uses the full backup directly. The procedure is: restore the nightly snapshot into a scratch database, verify the snapshot's checksum manifest before reading anything out of it, extract only that tenant's rows through the export tool, and import them into production inside one transaction with foreign keys deferred. Restoring the whole backup over production has been proposed twice under time pressure and refused both times: other tenants have written since the snapshot, and their data would be rolled back silently. The scratch database is torn down afterwards rather than kept, because it holds every tenant's data.

entries.text_original: Aurora's admin panel needs server-side pagination on the audit log page before the next compliance review. The page currently loads the full log for the selected period and paginates in the browser, which is fine for a day and unusable for a quarter — the largest tenant's quarterly log is about 1.2 million rows and the request times out well before rendering. Auditors ask for quarterly views specifically, so the current behaviour fails exactly the case the page exists for. The work is straightforward except for one detail: the existing filter UI builds its query client-side, so the filter grammar has to be expressed on the server without changing what users type.

entries.text_original: The intermittent duplicate charges in Aurora are suspected to originate in the payment provider's retry rather than in our own code: their webhook is delivered twice with different delivery ids but the same event id, and our handler deduplicates on delivery id. That would explain why duplicates cluster around provider-side incidents rather than around our deploys, and why the duplicated charges are always exactly one repeat rather than a storm. The alternative explanation, a race in our own idempotency table, would produce duplicates proportional to concurrency, and the data does not show that. Verifying it needs only a query grouping stored webhooks by event id.

entries.text_original: Aurora runs integration tests against a real PostgreSQL in a container rather than against an in-memory substitute. The substitute was faster and was used for two years, until a release passed every test and then failed in production on a query that used a window function the substitute silently accepted and evaluated differently. The team accepted the slower suite — about four minutes against forty seconds — in exchange for the guarantee that a passing test means the query works on the engine that will run it. Containers are reused across the suite with per-test schemas rather than per-test containers, which is what keeps the cost to minutes instead of tens of minutes.

entries.text_original: Aurora's session cookie is issued without the Domain attribute, so it is host-only and is not sent to the api subdomain. Every API call therefore relies on the bearer token in the Authorization header, which is intentional, but it also means a user who is logged in on the marketing site is not logged in on the docs site even though both are served from the same apex domain. Support reads that as a bug and it is filed as one roughly monthly. The behaviour is deliberate: a shared-domain cookie would be readable by every subdomain, including the ones that host user-uploaded content, and that is exactly the boundary the current setup keeps.

entries.text_original: Aurora keeps its background jobs in the same repository and the same deployable as the API rather than splitting them into a worker service. The split was proposed and declined: the jobs share the domain model closely enough that a split would have duplicated it or required a shared library with its own release cycle, and the team is not large enough to carry that. Isolation is achieved at runtime instead — the same image runs with a different command and its own resource limits, so a runaway job cannot starve request handling. The decision is documented as reversible if job count grows past the point where their deploy cadence conflicts with the API's.

entries.text_original: Public error responses in Aurora carry a stable machine-readable code and never expose an internal message. The code is what clients branch on, and it is treated as part of the API contract: renaming one is a breaking change requiring a new version. Internal detail goes to the log with the same correlation id that the response returns, so support can find it without the customer seeing it. The rule exists because an internal message once leaked a database constraint name that revealed a partner's table layout, and because clients had begun matching on message text, which then broke on a typo fix in a patch release.

entries.text_original: Publishing a breaking change to Aurora's partner API follows a fixed sequence: announce it in the partner changelog at least sixty days ahead, ship the new version alongside the old one, add a deprecation header to every response of the old version naming the sunset date, and only then, after both the date has passed and the old version's traffic has been below one percent for two consecutive weeks, remove it. The traffic condition is what actually gates removal, not the date — twice a partner has needed an extension, and honouring the date alone would have broken them on schedule rather than protecting them.

entries.text_original: Aurora's search relevance needs a labelled evaluation set before any further tuning. Right now changes to ranking are judged by eyeballing a handful of queries, which means a change that helps the queries someone happened to try and hurts everything else is indistinguishable from a real improvement. The plan is two hundred queries drawn from real logs, stratified by length and by whether they contain a product code, each with a single hand-labelled correct result. The labelling is the expensive part and is estimated at a week of a category manager's time, which is why it needs scheduling rather than being squeezed in.

entries.text_original: The gradual slowdown of Aurora's nightly report job is suspected to come from index bloat on the events table rather than from data growth: the row count has grown by about fifteen percent this year while the job's runtime has doubled, and a REINDEX on a copy of the table brought a representative query back to its old plan cost. The table sees heavy update traffic on a single column, which is exactly the pattern that leaves dead tuples in the index. If this is right the fix is a scheduled reindex rather than any change to the query, and the check is cheap: compare index size against the theoretical size for the current row count.

entries.text_original: Aurora serves product images through a CDN with a content-addressed path rather than a mutable one. An image's URL contains a hash of its bytes, so a replaced image is a new URL and no cache invalidation is needed anywhere. The alternative, a stable path plus purge calls, was used until a purge failed silently during a campaign and a discontinued product's photo stayed visible for two days. Content addressing costs a database column per image and makes the URL ugly, both of which were judged cheaper than the class of bug where cached content and current content disagree with nothing to detect it.

entries.text_original: Aurora's rate limiter counts a request at the gateway before authentication runs, so an unauthenticated client can exhaust an authenticated client's budget when both share an egress IP. This affects exactly one deployment shape — a corporate customer behind a single NAT whose employees also browse the public catalogue — and it presents as sporadic 429s for logged-in users with no visible cause. The counter's placement is not an oversight: counting after authentication would let an unauthenticated flood reach the auth service unmetered. The intended fix is a second, tighter bucket for unauthenticated traffic rather than moving the existing one.

entries.text_original: Any change to Aurora's pricing logic requires a second reviewer from outside the authoring team. The rule is narrow on purpose — it applies to the pricing module only, not to the whole codebase — and it exists because pricing bugs are the only class here that costs money per minute rather than degrading an experience. The outside reviewer is not expected to know the code; their job is to ask what the change does to a concrete order and to check that a test encodes that answer. Two of the three pricing incidents in the last year would have been caught by that question alone, which is what settled the argument about the overhead.

entries.text_original: Handling a suspected data leak in Aurora starts with preserving evidence, not with closing the hole. The order is: snapshot the relevant logs to immutable storage, record the exact time window and the accounts involved, notify the security owner, and only then rotate credentials or block access. Rotating first destroys the trail that tells you what was reached, and that has happened once here — the incident was contained in twenty minutes and it took three weeks to establish scope afterwards. The one exception is an active, ongoing exfiltration, where containment comes first and the runbook says so explicitly rather than leaving it to judgement.

entries.text_original: Aurora's staging environment needs its own copy of the search index rather than pointing at production's. The work is mostly plumbing — a second index name and a nightly reindex from anonymised data — but the anonymisation is the part that needs care: product data is not sensitive, yet the index also holds internal notes that must not leave production.

entries.text_original: Aurora's team decided against a service mesh. The evaluation ran for three weeks against a realistic staging topology and the conclusion was that the mesh solved two problems the system has — retries with budgets, and mTLS — while introducing an operational surface larger than either. mTLS was solved separately and directly; retry budgets were implemented in the shared client library, which every service already depends on. The decision records the condition under which it should be revisited: more than thirty services, or a second language in the fleet, whichever comes first, because both are the point where a shared library stops being the cheaper option.

entries.text_original: Aurora's primary database runs with synchronous_commit on for the orders schema and off for the analytics schema. The split was measured rather than assumed: turning it off for orders improved write throughput by about eighteen percent and was rejected immediately, because the failure mode is a committed order that is not durable. For analytics the same setting is fine — a lost row costs a gap in a chart that the next load fills in — and it removes roughly a third of the write latency on the heaviest ingest path.

entries.text_original: Bringing an Aurora region back after a full outage follows an order that is not obvious and is therefore written down. Databases first, and only to a read-only state; then the cache layer, warmed from the read-only primaries; then stateless services at zero traffic weight; then health verification against synthetic traffic; and only then the databases are promoted to writable and real traffic is admitted in twenty-percent steps. Admitting traffic before the cache is warm has been tried, in an actual incident, and it extended the outage by roughly forty minutes because the cold cache pushed the just-recovered database straight back into saturation.

entries.text_original: Aurora treats a flaky test as a failing test. There is no quarantine list and no automatic retry in CI, and both have been proposed. The argument that settled it was empirical: during the six months when a retry-once policy was in effect, the number of tests that were flaky grew steadily, because a test that fails one run in twenty is invisible under retry and nobody fixes what they cannot see. Deleting a flaky test is an acceptable outcome and is preferred to leaving it retrying.

entries.text_original: Aurora needs to replace its hand-rolled feature-flag evaluation cache. The current implementation refreshes every thirty seconds by re-fetching the entire ruleset, which is fine at the present size and will not be at ten times it. More pressingly, a failed refresh currently falls back to the last known ruleset with no upper bound on staleness, so a flag turned off during an incident may stay on in a pod whose refresh has been failing quietly. The replacement should stream updates and treat prolonged staleness as an error worth alerting on.

entries.text_original: Aurora's checkout conversion drop on Safari may be caused by the third-party fraud-detection script rather than by anything in the checkout code. The drop starts on the day the script's vendor shipped a new version, it is confined to Safari, and the script is known to use a storage API that Safari partitions differently. Nothing in our own release history lines up. The test is straightforward and cheap: disable the script for a small Safari cohort for a week and compare, which requires only a flag the checkout already reads.

An earlier sequential scheme leaked order volume to anyone who placed two orders and subtracted, which a competitor is known to have done, and the migration away from it was one of the more painful ones in this system's history because the old identifiers appeared in printed documents.

A rejected request with a named unknown field is a worse first experience and a much better second one.
